description: The preimage discriminator for receipt anchor batches. A SynOI gateway timestamps ONE of two preimages per Merkle batch: the raw 32-byte RFC 6962 root when the SynOI counter-signature was unavailable, or SHA-256 of the utf-8 counter-signed canonical bundle when it succeeded. The two values are different, so a verifier not told which one was submitted has to guess and rejects a valid OpenTimestamps proof roughly half the time. Every anchor batch therefore publishes ots.digest_kind and ots.digest_sha256. Batches written before that field existed publish digest_kind 'unknown': the timestamped preimage was never recorded, and an implementation MUST report that rather than assume either form. All hashes are bare lowercase hex, no sha256: prefix.

constants.merkle_root_rule: digest_kind 'merkle_root' -> the submitted digest is the raw 32 bytes of merkle_root itself. digest_sha256 === merkle_root.
constants.countersign_rule: digest_kind 'countersign_bundle_sha256' -> the submitted digest is SHA-256(utf8(synoi.canonical_bundle)). digest_sha256 === that hash, and it does NOT equal merkle_root.
constants.unknown_rule: ots_proof present with no digest_kind -> report 'unknown'. Do NOT backfill, do NOT default to merkle_root, and do NOT report a recomputation mismatch as tampering.
constants.no_timestamp_rule: ots_proof absent -> digest_kind is null, meaning nothing was timestamped. This is distinct from 'unknown'.

cases.name: countersigned_bundle_anchor
cases.note: Counter-signing succeeded, so the OTS proof commits to the bundle hash, not to the root. A verifier that assumed merkle_root here would compute a mismatch on an entirely valid proof.

cases.name: merkle_root_anchor
cases.note: The control plane was unreachable, so the OTS proof commits to the raw Merkle root. Same batch shape as above; only the kind and the digest differ.

cases.name: legacy_unknown_preimage
cases.note: A batch anchored before the discriminator existed. The OTS proof is real; which preimage it covers was never recorded. The honest verdict is not-recomputable, and a mismatch against either candidate is NOT a tampering finding.

cases.name: no_timestamp
cases.note: The batch was recorded but never submitted to a calendar. Distinct from unknown: there is nothing to recompute because nothing was timestamped.
